I remember playing this on coolmathgames.com back in the day and I had quite a bit of fun (even though I was absolutely terrible at it) so I felt it was only fair that I get the game on steam to both support the developer and relive an old memory.

This game has a very interesting and satisfying movement mechanic and I'm a sucker for movement based games. The ship is really nice to control and the fine movements required to carefully land it on each planet are really fun to master.

The game is quite short and after 98 minutes I've already beat 4 of the 5 levels in the game although part of that could be that I skipped the portion of the game where you have no idea how to properly control the ship due to the fact that I've played this game before.

Even so, once you get used to the movement the game is quite easy to beat (except for the last level which, I'll admit, has quite a high spike in difficulty), so for some people the price might not be worth it.

The game can also be quite unforgiving with the damage system being so sensitive. It does make it annoying at times but it also helps to make it that much more satisfying when you pull off a perfect landing.

Overall, it's not perfect and there's definitely some room for improvement but I like this game and think there's a lot of fun to be had in it.

A very basic game, asteroids has more complicated controls.  You are a little ship that can only thrust, turn left and turn right, nothing else at all.  The game itself consists of leaving a dead world and colonizing a new world which is one particular planet you must reach at the end of the level.  Your ship has fuel, oxygen and a hull.  If any of these get to 0 you die, you can replenish these by landing on planets with the right materials where most planets have all three in at least small quantities and many have all three in abundance.  Also along the way you need to pick up terraforming materials which you get from certain special planets.  You only need to do this once but additional materials give you a better ending planet and a higher score.  Also there are a few planets that have colonists you can rescue, just land on it for a certain amount of time with similar effects.

So the game is basically move from planet to planet to survive and get materials avoiding danger (landing damage, asteroids, moons, black hole, suns and enemies) and get a high score if you care.  A lot of the game is just landing safely, you must come in slowly and avoid mountains and water.  Once you get good at that, the game is mildly fun... except for the last level which is very, very hard.  In that level you start on an enemy planet and are immediately attacked by swarms of enemies (a very, very rare occurrence in the all the previous levels).  Now you have to not only avoid them, but safely land on planets, avoid many obstacles (seems like more than previous levels), etc.  I tried this level probably 50 times (not counting immediate deaths because I was distracted at the beginning of the game... it restarts automatically) and couldn't beat it.  I came very close once, and fairly close maybe 5 other times but in the end I decided it wasn't worth the effort and gave up.  It's beatable for sure, just need some luck, skill and a lot of patience.

Frankly the game is too simple, too short and too hard on the final level for me to recommend.  It isn't bad, just not really worth the time in my opinion.

Great little gem.  The perfect snack-size game between bigger, stodgier gaming affairs.
You power your little spaceship, without weapons, across space in a 2D plane, periodically stopping off at planets to recharge your oxygen supplies and refuel, all the while dodging moons, asteroids, meteorites, black holes, scorching suns, space bandits, and of course, avoiding slamming head-long into the planet you were trying to land on.  

You begin each map on a dead planet, and on some planets you pick up biological samples that will allow you to terraform your destination planet, and you can also pick up other survivors of the vaguely specified earth apocalypse.  This has no real tangible benefit beyond your score, and the blurb you get when you complete a map by landing on the destination planet, but it's all effective in adding window dressing to the simplistic style of the game, and giving you the sense that the future of the human race rests on your shoulders.
Your only controls are a single button to power your thrusters, and the 2 arrow keys to alter the direction of the thrust and thus steer the ship.  The developers have done a very commendable job in getting the controls to feel just right, and the added challenge of bracing against and adjusting to handle the gravitational pull of planets as you get closer adds just that little something extra in terms of challenge and your level of engagement.
The game is not a cake-walk but every attempt you will feel yourself getting better, and you naturally start to figure out how to handle situations better in the future.  Beating the final mission had me having a nail shredding ending, my fuel tank empty, blasting out the last of my oxygen as backup thrust to steer myself into a pretty heavy landing that shredded most of my ship's health.  But I survived, and won the game.  A proper fist-pump in the air moment!
There's 2 hours of gaming bliss here across 5 progressively more challenging maps.  Get it, you will not regret it!
